results.title: Strongly embedded subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $M$ of a group $X$ is strongly embedded in $X$ if $M \ne X$, the order of $M$ is even, and for every $g \in X$ outside $M$ the order of $M \cap g M g^{-1}$ is odd. Here an infinite group is assigned order $0$, so an infinite $M$ counts as having even order and an infinite intersection never has odd order.

results.title: The group $\mathrm{PSL}(2, 2^n)$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n \ge 1$, $\mathrm{PSL}(2, 2^n)$ is the projective special linear group of $2 \times 2$ matrices over the Galois field $\mathrm{GF}(2^n)$. For $n = 0$ the same construction is taken over $\mathrm{GF}(2)$ instead.

results.title: The Suzuki group $\mathrm{Sz}(2^{2n+1})$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Suzuki group $\mathrm{Sz}(2^{2n+1})$ is the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}(4, \mathrm{GF}(2^{2n+1}))$ generated by the matrices in the generating set of the Suzuki group (all of which are invertible).

results.title: The group $\mathrm{PSU}(3, 2^n)$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$, let $q = 2^n$ and let $J$ be the $3 \times 3$ matrix with ones on the antidiagonal and zeros elsewhere. Then $\mathrm{PSU}(3, q)$ is the image in the projective general linear group $\mathrm{PGL}(3, \mathrm{GF}(q^2))$ of the group of matrices $A \in \mathrm{GL}(3, \mathrm{GF}(q^2))$ with $\det A = 1$ and $\bar{A}^{\mathsf{T}} J A = J$, where $\bar{A}$ is obtained from $A$ by applying $z \mapsto z^q$…

results.title: Simple Bender groups
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A group $G$ is a simple Bender group if it is isomorphic to $\mathrm{PSL}(2, 2^n)$ for some $n \ge 2$, to the Suzuki group $\mathrm{Sz}(2^{2n+1})$ for some $n \ge 1$, or to $\mathrm{PSU}(3, 2^n)$ for some $n \ge 2$.

results.title: Bender–Suzuki theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a finite simple group that has a strongly embedded subgroup $M$. Then $X$ is a simple Bender group: $X$ is isomorphic to $\mathrm{PSL}(2, 2^n)$ for some $n \ge 2$, to the Suzuki group $\mathrm{Sz}(2^{2n+1})$ for some $n \ge 1$, or to $\mathrm{PSU}(3, 2^n)$ for some $n \ge 2$.

results.summary: A class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups is a formation if every group in $\mathfrak{X}$ is finite, $\mathfrak{X}$ contains the trivial group, for every finite group $G$ in $\mathfrak{X}$ and every normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ the quotient $G/N$ lies in $\mathfrak{X}$, and for every finite group $G$ with normal subgroups $N_1$ and $N_2$ such that $G/N_1$ and $G/N_2$ lie in $\mathfrak{X}$, the quotient $G/(N_1 \cap N_2)$ lies…

results.title: Inclusion of group classes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For classes of groups $\mathfrak{X}$ and $\mathfrak{Y}$, the class $\mathfrak{X}$ is included in $\mathfrak{Y}$, written $\mathfrak{X} \subseteq \mathfrak{Y}$, if every group that belongs to $\mathfrak{X}$ also belongs to $\mathfrak{Y}$.

results.title: Complete lattices of formations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $\Theta$ of classes of groups is a complete lattice of formations if it is nonempty, every member of $\Theta$ is a formation, for every nonempty subset $S \subseteq \Theta$ the intersection of the classes in $S$ (the class of groups belonging to every member of $S$) belongs to $\Theta$, and $\Theta$ has a member that contains every member of $\Theta$.

results.title: Joins in a set of group classes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\Theta$ and $S$ be sets of classes of groups. A class $\mathfrak{J}$ is the join of $S$ in $\Theta$ if $\mathfrak{J} \in \Theta$, every member of $S$ is contained in $\mathfrak{J}$, and $\mathfrak{J}$ is contained in every member of $\Theta$ that contains every member of $S$.

results.title: Compact elements of a set of group classes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\Theta$ be a set of classes of groups and $\mathfrak{A}$ a class of groups. Then $\mathfrak{A}$ is compact in $\Theta$ if, for every subset $S \subseteq \Theta$ and every join $\mathfrak{J}$ of $S$ in $\Theta$ with $\mathfrak{A} \subseteq \mathfrak{J}$, there are a finite subset $S_1 \subseteq S$ and a join $\mathfrak{J}_1$ of $S_1$ in $\Theta$ with $\mathfrak{A} \subseteq \mathfrak{J}_1$.

results.title: Algebraic sets of group classes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $\Theta$ of classes of groups is algebraic if every member $\mathfrak{A}$ of $\Theta$ is the join in $\Theta$ of some subset $S \subseteq \Theta$ all of whose members are compact in $\Theta$.

results.title: Modular sets of group classes

results.summary: A set $\Theta$ of classes of groups is modular if for all $\mathfrak{A}, \mathfrak{B}, \mathfrak{C} \in \Theta$ with $\mathfrak{A} \subseteq \mathfrak{C}$ the following holds: whenever $\mathfrak{J}_1$ is the join in $\Theta$ of the set $\{\mathfrak{A}, \mathfrak{B} \cap \mathfrak{C}\}$ and $\mathfrak{D}$ is the join in $\Theta$ of the set $\{\mathfrak{A}, \mathfrak{B}\}$, the classes $\mathfrak{J}_1$ and…

results.title: Kourovka Problem 18.92(a) (A. N. Skiba)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that some set $\Theta$ of classes of groups is a complete lattice of formations of finite groups and is not algebraic.

results.title: The non-modular formation lattice problem (Kourovka 18.92(b), A. N. Skiba)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that there is a complete lattice of formations of finite groups that is not modular, joins being least upper bounds in the lattice and meets being intersections.

results.title: Non-algebraic complete lattices of formations exist
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a set $\Theta$ of classes of groups that is a complete lattice of formations of finite groups and is not algebraic; that is, Kourovka Problem 18.92(a) has a positive answer.

results.title: A non-modular complete lattice of formations exists (Kourovka 18.92(b))
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a complete lattice of formations of finite groups that is not modular: a nonempty set $\Theta$ of formations of finite groups, ordered by inclusion, that contains the intersection of each of its nonempty subsets and has a largest element, in which the modular law $A \vee (B \wedge C) = (A \vee B) \wedge C$ for $A \le C$ fails, joins being least upper bounds in $\Theta$ and meets intersections.

results.title: Class of finite groups (Kourovka 13.51)
results.caption: Abbreviation

results.title: Intersection of classes of finite groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For classes $\mathfrak F_1$ and $\mathfrak F_2$ of finite groups, their intersection $\mathfrak F_1 \cap \mathfrak F_2$ is the class of finite groups $G$ with $G \in \mathfrak F_1$ and $G \in \mathfrak F_2$. For formations $\mathfrak F_1$ and $\mathfrak F_2$ it is their meet in the lattice of formations.

results.title: Join of formations (Kourovka 13.51)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For classes $\mathfrak F_1$ and $\mathfrak F_2$ of finite groups, their formation join is the class of finite groups $G$ that belong to every formation containing all groups of $\mathfrak F_1$ and of $\mathfrak F_2$: the intersection of all formations containing $\mathfrak F_1 \cup \mathfrak F_2$, which is the smallest such formation. For formations $\mathfrak F_1$ and $\mathfrak F_2$ it is their join in the…

results.title: Kourovka Problem 13.51 (Skiba): finite modular lattices embed in the lattice of formations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every finite modular lattice $L$ there is an injective map $f$ from $L$ to the formations of finite groups such that, for all $a, b \in L$, $f(a \wedge b) = f(a) \cap f(b)$ and $f(a \vee b)$ is the smallest formation containing $f(a) \cup f(b)$.

results.title: Not every finite modular lattice embeds in the lattice of formations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a finite modular lattice $L$ that admits no injective map $f$ from $L$ to the formations of finite groups such that, for all $a, b \in L$, $f(a \wedge b) = f(a) \cap f(b)$ and $f(a \vee b)$ is the smallest formation containing $f(a) \cup f(b)$. This answers Kourovka Problem 13.51 (Skiba) in the negative.

results.title: Inclusion of classes of finite groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For classes $\mathfrak{F}$ and $\mathfrak{G}$ of finite groups, $\mathfrak{F} \subseteq \mathfrak{G}$ means that every finite group in $\mathfrak{F}$ belongs to $\mathfrak{G}$.

results.title: Local formation of finite groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A class $\mathfrak{F}$ of finite groups is a local formation when it is a formation, contains the trivial group, and is saturated: a finite group $G$ belongs to $\mathfrak{F}$ whenever $G/\Phi(G)$ does, where $\Phi(G)$ is the Frattini subgroup of $G$.

results.title: Residual of a finite group with respect to a class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a class $\mathfrak{F}$ of finite groups and a finite group $G$, the $\mathfrak{F}$-residual $G^{\mathfrak{F}}$ is the intersection of all normal subgroups $N$ of $G$ with $G/N \in \mathfrak{F}$.

results.title: Classes of finite groups (Kourovka 10.56)
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A class of finite groups is given by its membership predicate: a proposition about each finite group, true exactly for the members of the class.

results.title: Formations of finite groups (Kourovka 10.56)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A class $X$ of finite groups is a formation if it is closed under isomorphism, contains the trivial group, contains $G/N$ whenever it contains $G$ and $N$ is a normal subgroup of $G$, and is closed under subdirect products: if $N_1$ and $N_2$ are normal subgroups of a finite group $G$ with $G/N_1 \in X$ and $G/N_2 \in X$, then $G/(N_1 \cap N_2) \in X$.

results.title: Formations of nilpotent groups of class at most 4
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A class $X$ of finite groups is a formation of nilpotent groups of class at most $4$ if $X$ is a formation and every group $G$ in $X$ is nilpotent of class at most $4$, that is, the fourth term $\zeta_4(G)$ of the upper central series of $G$ is all of $G$.

results.title: Intersection of classes of finite groups (Kourovka 10.56)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The meet of two classes $X$ and $Y$ of finite groups is their intersection $X \cap Y$: the class of finite groups that belong to both $X$ and $Y$.

results.title: Formation generated by two classes (Kourovka 10.56)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For classes $X$ and $Y$ of finite groups, the formation generated by $X \cup Y$ is the class of finite groups that belong to every formation containing both $X$ and $Y$. For formations $X$ and $Y$ it is their join in the lattice of formations.

results.title: The distributivity question for nilpotent class-4 formations (Kourovka 10.56)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For all formations $A$, $B$, $C$ of finite nilpotent groups of class at most $4$, a finite group lies in $A \cap (B \vee C)$ if and only if it lies in $(A \cap B) \vee (A \cap C)$, where $X \vee Y$ denotes the formation generated by $X \cup Y$. That is, the lattice of formations of finite nilpotent groups of class at most $4$ is distributive (A. N. Skiba).

results.title: The lattice of nilpotent class-4 formations is not distributive (Kourovka 10.56)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist formations $A$, $B$, $C$ of finite nilpotent groups of class at most $4$ such that the classes $A \cap (B \vee C)$ and $(A \cap B) \vee (A \cap C)$ differ, that is, some finite group lies in exactly one of them; here $X \vee Y$ denotes the formation generated by $X \cup Y$, the intersection of all formations containing $X$ and $Y$.

results.summary: For a ring $R$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, a matrix $\tau \in \mathrm{GL}_n(R)$ is an elementary transvection when $\tau = 1 + r e_{ij}$ for some indices $i \ne j$ and some nonzero $r \in R$, where $e_{ij}$ is the matrix unit with $1$ in position $(i, j)$ and $0$ elsewhere.

results.title: The multiplication operator on continuous functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$ be a compact topological space, let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C(X, \mathbb{K})$ be the Banach algebra of continuous functions $X \to \mathbb{K}$ with the supremum norm. For $\varphi \in C(X, \mathbb{K})$, the multiplication operator $M_\varphi$ is the bounded linear operator on $C(X, \mathbb{K})$ given by $M_\varphi f = \varphi f$.

results.title: Multiplication by a constant on continuous functions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a compact topological space, let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$. The multiplication operator on $C(X, \mathbb{K})$ by the constant function with value $\mu$ equals $\mu$ times the identity operator.

results.title: Spectrum of a multiplication operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a compact topological space, let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $\varphi \in C(X, \mathbb{K})$. The spectrum of the multiplication operator $M_\varphi f = \varphi f$, as an element of the algebra of bounded linear operators on $C(X, \mathbb{K})$, is the range $\varphi(X)$ of $\varphi$.

results.title: Invertibility of a multiplication operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a compact topological space, let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $\varphi \in C(X, \mathbb{K})$. The multiplication operator $M_\varphi f = \varphi f$ is invertible in the algebra of bounded linear operators on $C(X, \mathbb{K})$ if and only if $\varphi(x) \neq 0$ for every $x \in X$.

results.title: Eigenvalues of a multiplication operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff space, let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\varphi \in C(X, \mathbb{K})$ and let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$. Then $\mu$ is an eigenvalue of the multiplication operator $M_\varphi f = \varphi f$ on $C(X, \mathbb{K})$ if and only if the level set $\varphi^{-1}(\{\mu\})$ has nonempty interior.

results.title: Log-space computable functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f$ from bitstrings to bitstrings is log-space computable when there are a constant $c \in \mathbb{N}$ and a time bound $t : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that some multi-tape Turing machine with binary alphabet and finitely many states, on every bitstring input $x$, halts with output $f(x)$ within $t(|x|)$ steps and visits at most $c \lfloor \log_2(|x| + 1) \rfloor + c$ work-tape cells in total.

results.title: Log-space many-one reductions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A decision problem $L_1$ is log-space many-one reducible to a decision problem $L_2$ when there is a log-space computable function $f$ from bitstrings to bitstrings such that, for every bitstring $x$, $L_1(x)$ is true if and only if $L_2(f(x))$ is true.

results.title: Nondeterministic decision
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine $M$ over the boolean alphabet decides a set $L$ of bitstrings if, for every bitstring $x$, $x \in L$ if and only if some computation path of $M$ on $x$ ends in a halted configuration whose output is the one-element list $[\mathrm{true}]$.

results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A gate of a flat Boolean circuit on $n$ inputs is one of: an input variable $x_i$ for some $i < n$; a Boolean constant; a negation gate with one predecessor index $a \in \mathbb{N}$; a conjunction gate or a disjunction gate with a list of predecessor indices; or a mod gate with a modulus $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list of predecessor indices.

results.title: Predecessors of a gate
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Well-formed flat circuits
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Depth of a flat Boolean circuit
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Circuits without mod gates
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Monotone circuits
results.caption: Definition

results.title: The parity language
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The parity decision problem accepts a bitstring exactly when an odd number of its entries are true.

results.title: The majority language
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The majority language is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ has more true bits than false bits, that is, when $2k > |x|$, where $k$ is the number of true bits of $x$ and $|x|$ is its length.

results.title: The class coRP
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The class coRP. coRP is the class of decision problems $L$ whose complement, the decision problem that accepts exactly the bitstrings that $L$ rejects, belongs to RP.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A decision problem $L$ belongs to $\mathsf{coRP}$ if and only if its complement, the decision problem that accepts exactly the bitstrings $L$ rejects, belongs to $\mathsf{RP}$.

results.title: ZPP is contained in RP

results.title: ZPP is contained in coRP

results.title: The class NC
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: $\mathsf{NC}$ is the complexity class of decision problems that belong to $\mathsf{NC}^k$ for some natural number $k$, that is, $\mathsf{NC} = \bigcup_{k} \mathsf{NC}^k$.

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: The NC hierarchy is increasing

results.title: Computational basis state of a bitstring
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Tensor product of state vectors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For vectors $\varphi \in \mathbb{C}^{2^a}$ and $\psi \in \mathbb{C}^{2^b}$, indexed by $\{0, \dots, 2^a - 1\}$ and $\{0, \dots, 2^b - 1\}$, their tensor product is the vector in $\mathbb{C}^{2^{a+b}}$ whose entry at $s$ is $\varphi_{s \bmod 2^a}\, \psi_{\lfloor s / 2^a \rfloor}$. Thus $\varphi$ occupies the low-order $a$ bits of the index and $\psi$ the high-order $b$ bits.

results.title: All-zero state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The all-zero state on $a$ qubits is the vector in $\mathbb{C}^{2^a}$, indexed by $s \in \{0, \dots, 2^a - 1\}$, whose entry at $s = 0$ is $1$ and whose other entries are $0$; that is, the computational basis state $|0 \cdots 0\rangle$.

results.title: Squared norm of a state vector
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a vector $\psi \in \mathbb{C}^{2^m}$, indexed by $\{0, \dots, 2^m - 1\}$, its squared norm is the real number $\sum_{s} \overline{\psi_s}\, \psi_s = \sum_{s} |\psi_s|^2$.

results.title: Acceptance probability of a quantum state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a state vector $\psi$ on $N$ qubits, given by its amplitudes $\psi(s) \in \mathbb{C}$ at the basis states $s \in \{0, \dots, 2^N - 1\}$, the acceptance probability is the sum of $|\psi(s)|^2$ over the basis states $s$ whose qubit $0$ (the output qubit, the least significant bit of $s$) equals $1$. By the Born rule, for a unit vector $\psi$ this is the probability that measuring the output qubit gives $1$.

results.title: Mean fitness under Hardy–Weinberg proportions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Mean fitness under Hardy–Weinberg with LoF frequency `q` and fitnesses `1, 1 - s, 1 - t`: `1 - 2 q (1 - q) s - q² t`.

results.title: Loss-of-function frequency after selection
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: LoF frequency after selection: `q (1 - s (1 - q) - t q) / w̄`.

results.title: One diploid generation of selection and mutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: One generation: selection, then mutation of wild-type alleles at rate `U`.

results.title: Mean fitness under multiplicative fitness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With multiplicative fitness, `w̄ = (1 - s q)²` for every `q`.

results.title: `U / s` is an equilibrium
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `U / s` is an equilibrium of the multiplicative diploid model (an algebraic identity for `s ≠ 0`, `U ≠ 1`; a frequency in `[0, 1]` when `0 ≤ U ≤ s`).

results.title: Mean fitness at the multiplicative mutation–selection equilibrium
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At the multiplicative equilibrium the mean fitness is `(1 - U)²`, independent of `s`. Requires `U ≠ 1`, so that `U / s` is genuinely a fixed point (`diploidStep_mult_fixed`): for `U = 1` the point `U / s` is not an equilibrium.

results.title: Haldane–Muller load
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `1 - w̄ = 2U - U²` at the multiplicative equilibrium (`U ≠ 1`, so `U / s` is a fixed point).

results.title: Positivity of mean fitness for allele frequencies below one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Mean fitness is positive for `0 ≤ q < 1` and `s, t ≤ 1` (nonnegative fitnesses).

results.title: Equilibria lie at or below `U / s`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Equilibria lie at or below `U / s` when homozygotes are at least multiplicatively unfit (`2s - s² ≤ t`, which includes recessive lethality `t = 1`): every fixed point `q ∈ [0, 1)` of the diploid map satisfies `q ≤ U / s`.
